newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAFRICA FIRST FOOD SAYS KEEN INTEREST IN SHR OFFER.
newsitem.headline: SAFRICA FIRST FOOD SAYS KEEN INTEREST IN SHR OFFER.

text.p: First SA Food Holdings, the South African food group which will list on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in June, said on Thursday institutions and company employees had shown keen interest in its share offer.
Corrie Roodt, managing director of First Food holding company, First South African Holdings (FSAH), said institutions had already snapped up 20 million First Food shares in a private placement.
"We were exceptionally pleased with the reception we received and the placement was accordingly more than 5.5 times subscribed, with every institution approached applying for shares," Roodt said.
First Food management and employees were offered 12.5 million shares. "And we were delighted to receive applications for more than 14 million shares," Roodt said.
He said the listing of First Food, which invests in niched food manufacturing operations, will raise capital to pursue a number of expansion opportunities that existed in the marketplace.

After the listing FSAH, which is a sibling of Nasdaq-quoted First South Africa Corp , is expected to hold a 70 percent stake in First Food. Employees and management will hold 10 percent, with the public the remainder.

John Welch, First Foods' managing director said he expects that the upper end market for the group's products will expand rapidly due to growing urbanisation, an increase in dual income houselholds, an expanding middle class and a lifestyle trend towards increased consumption of convenience foods.
First Food owns four operating companies, namely Piemans Pantry, Astoria Bakery, Seemann's Quality Meat Products and Gull Food.
The company's prospectus is expected to be issued around May 8.
